veranderings.rede: Two main clauses with their own subject and verb joined by 'en' take a comma (AWS 2017); the protected wording is left intact.

veranderings.voor: in die son en word hulle meer werd
veranderings.na: in die son, en word hulle meer werd
veranderings.rede: The second clause has its own subject ('hulle') and verb, so a comma goes before 'en' (AWS 2017).
Many beans each have a shell, so the plural 'doppe' reads more naturally.

veranderings.blok: Waar die wins die opvallendste is
veranderings.voor: voor die meeste waarde bygevoeg is
veranderings.na: voordat die meeste waarde bygevoeg word
veranderings.rede: 'Voordat' is the standard written conjunction, and the present passive 'bygevoeg word' fits the sequence better than the perfect 'bygevoeg is'.

veranderings.voor: Gisting is wanneer klein lewende dinge kos of sap verander.
veranderings.na: Die proses waarin klein lewende dinge kos of sap verander.
veranderings.rede: 'X is wanneer' copies the English 'X is when'; a noun-phrase definition matches the other glossary entries and keeps the meaning.

vlae.teks: Die boer sny die ryp pod van die boom
vlae.rede: 'Pod' is English; Afrikaans usually says 'peul' (or 'kakaopeul'). It is also the glossary headword, so it cannot be changed here; a writer or person should decide whether the term itself changes.
One pours a mixture into moulds, not into blocks, so the phrase is unidiomatic; fixing it means naming the moulds, which is a content choice for the writer.

vlae.teks: ver van die plase waar die hulpbron groei
vlae.rede: 'Die hulpbron' is vague here (it means the cocoa); 'die kakao' would be clearer, but 'hulpbron' may be a deliberate subject term, so the writer should decide.
